Prevention: Rotate cabbage with maize, beans, etc. every two years.
Ensure that the fields are free of weeds (as some weeds harbour aphids).
In the nursery, use correct spacing of 15cm apart per row.
In the field, use correct spacing of 60cm by 60cm for big headed varieties, such as drumhead, when transplanting.
Avoid application of broad spectrum pesticides such as
Abamectin in order to preserve natural enemies like ladybird beetles and parasitic wasps which assist in reducing the population of aphids.
Uproot and burn crop residues at the end of the harvest to prevent infestations spreading to the new planting.
Intercrop with garlic or onion to repel the aphids.
Inspect transplants before planting, ensure that they are not infested with aphids.
Monitoring: Scout for aphids on the underside of young leaves and in the interior of the cabbage head.
Begin scouting soon after transplanting and repeat once every week.
Check for stunting and curling of leaves once every week.
Direct Control: Uproot and burn severely infected plants.
Where available, cover the nursery with fleece or fine netting, and water without opening the covering.
Control with natural or organic sprays like soap and water mixture. 1 to 2 % solution.
Restrictions: Use personal protective equipment when handling and applying pesticides, follow the label recommendations.
Do not eat, drink, smoke when mixing or applying pesticides.
